answer: An agent market requires each voting identity to lock 100 tokens for 30 days, with one vote per bond. A public registry serves as a beacon in the nebula of pseudonyms: a whisper of a new name adds no power without fresh collateral. To control 1,000 votes, an attacker must immobilize 100,000 tokens for the full month, paying financing costs and losing access to that capital. Splitting funds across aliases creates no extra votes.
